text: Got it — the bug is in Interval.fromISO: it calls DateTime.fromISO/Duration.fromISO directly, which throw when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true, so duration-form inputs like "2016-05-25/PT1H" blow up instead of returning a valid Interval. I'm fixing it now (parse inside try/catch and branch on validity flags).

On it. The bug is in objToLocalTS (src/impl/util.js): for years 0-99 it re-applies the year after JS's 19XX interpretation, but not the month/day, so a day overflow that lands in February is resolved in the wrong calendar (2000 is a leap year, 100 isn't) and the result is off by a day. Fixing it now.

Request #1 is fixed and verified. Interval.fromISO now parses the start/end DateTimes (and durations) inside try/catch and branches on validity flags, so with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true, "2016-05-25/PT1H" and "PT1H/2016-05-25" return valid Intervals instead of throwing, while unparsable input still throws InvalidIntervalError. Full jest run: same 2 pre-existing failures (French-locale toFormat) as before my change, no new failures; all 127 interval tests pass.

On it. The isInDST getter compares this.offset against this.set({ month: 1 }) — but set() keeps the day of month, so for a DateTime that is itself in January (or May) the comparison is against the same instant and can never be greater, wrongly returning false. That's exactly the 1974 US case (DST ran Jan 6 – Oct 27), where January and May dates report false. Fixing it to compare against Jan 1.

Request #2 is fixed and verified. objToLocalTS now re-applies the month and day when correcting years 0-99 (d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)), so day overflows that pass through February are resolved in the correct calendar. DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 }) now gives 0100-03-02 (was 0100-03-01); the existing 100-barrier plus/minus tests still pass. Full jest run unchanged: only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.

On it. The conversion matrix in src/duration.js is missing the quarters→seconds entry in casualMatrix (every other entry, including accurateMatrix's quarters, has it), so converting quarters to seconds yields NaN. Adding it now.

On it. padStart in src/impl/util.js mishandles negative numbers — padStart(-5, 4) yields "00-5" instead of "-0005" — so toISODate() for a negative year comes out as "00-5-05-25" rather than "-0005-05-25". Fixing it to pad the absolute value and keep the sign.

Request #5 is fixed and verified. padStart now pads the absolute value and keeps the sign, so DateTime.fromObject({ year: -5, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate() returns "-0005-05-25" (was "00-5-05-25"); toISO() is "-0005-05-25T00:00:00.000Z", and the existing ±118040 / year-3 / 1982 cases still pass. Full jest run unchanged: only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.

On it. FixedOffsetZone hardcodes `get isValid() { return true; }`, so a zone constructed with a non-numeric offset (e.g. new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")) claims to be valid and any DateTime using it is wrongly valid too. Fixing it to `isNumber(this.fixed)`.

Request #3 is fixed and verified. isInDST now compares against this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }) instead of this.set({ month: 1 }), so a January (or May) DateTime no longer compares against itself. An hourly scan of all 8760 hours of 1974 in America/New_York now matches the real DST offset exactly (true from Jan 6 02:00 through Oct 27), and the existing LA pre/during/post-DST expectations still pass. Full jest run unchanged: only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.

Request #6 is fixed and verified. FixedOffsetZone.isValid now returns isNumber(this.fixed) instead of hardcoded true, so new FixedOffsetZone("blorp").isValid is false and a DateTime built with such a zone is itself invalid (its toISO() is null). UTC/instance(n)/parseSpecifier zones remain valid, and test/zones/fixedOffset.test.js still passes 7/7. Full jest run unchanged: only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.
